subject: Difference between Link Parameter in control.family and control.predictor

messages.author: 570097af2ad4ddd8
messages.subject: Difference between Link Parameter in control.family and control.predictor
parts:
Hello,

I am slightly confused about the link parameter in `inla` for `control.family` and `control.predictor`. From reading the FAQ, I understand that (feel free to correct if anything is inaccurate):

- `control.family(control.link = "<name of link function")`: determines the link function between the predictor `eta` and the mean `mu`, such as `identity`, `logit`, `log-link`, `log`, etc. We can see all the available links with `lapply(inla.models()$likelihood, function(x) x$link)`

- `control.predictor(link = 1)`: determines the index of the family which should use for computing the posterior of the distribution

My questions are:

1) If we are estimating a model with a single likelihood family (say, "gaussian"), do we still need to supply the link index to `control.predictor` or the default is to have `link = 1`? When do we need to supply an argument when we have an estimation with a single family?

2) The documentation says that if an element of the response vector is not null then the corresponding entry in `link` is ignored. Is this because it knows which family an observation which is not null belongs to? But if the later is true, why would it not know the corresponding family for those values which are null given that they are defined in the same dataset (say `Y`)?

3) We can always use `inla.marginal.transform` or any other function that operates on the posterior to estimate posterior predictions of the observations. On the other hand, we cannot easily add custom link functions to `control.family`, it has to be one of the listed options. Is that correct?

4) Is there anywhere in the docs an explanation about how to implement custom link functions for linking `eta` to the likelihood function?

Thanks in advance for your help.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Difference between Link Parameter in control.family and control.predictor
parts:
For 1) and 2), link is only needed for NA “observations”, but there is no harm in specifying it for actual observations. You are correct that for a single likelihood model, it would be reasonable for inla to infer that link=1 is intended for all elements, but there are use cases where this isn’t a reasonable assumption (when predicting parts of the linear predictor, for which the link function doesn’t make sense, and might result in NaN etc). For this and other historical reasons, the user must explicitly specify it.

3) yes, link functions need to be explicitly implemented. Marginal.transform isn’t as accurate as doing it within the inla call.

4) I’m not sure...

Finn

Thanks again for the quick reply!

Now I understand the `link` argument better. There is one thing which remains unclear after re-reading your answer and the FAQ.

When the `link` argument is not passed to `control.predictor`, INLA will use the identity link for the `NA` observations. In such cases, INLA even display a warning message.

However, how can INLA produce posterior for the fitted values using the identity link function in cases for which the likelihood is not defined? Let me give a concrete example to be clearer.

In the FAQ, the Tokyo dataset is used to illustrate prediction with INLA. The aim is to model the variable `y` using a binomial likelihood. The binomial likelihood is parameterised by a probability p which must be between 0 and 1. So if we use the identity link function for estimating the posterior of fitted values (that is, p(y | theta) ), it is not clear to me what is being estimated since the likelihood at values outside of the interval [0, 1] is not defined, or to be more precise it is 0. 

Thus, what kind of posterior is being estimated by INLA in this case, since p(y | theta) > 0 for values outside of the range of the Binomial distribution which is our assumption for p(y | theta). See the images attached for the case where we use the logit and the identity. These are two different observations from `result$marginals.fitted.values`.

Thanks again for the help.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Difference between Link Parameter in control.family and control.predictor
parts: On 3 May 2018 at 19:57, <guilherm...@flowminder.org> wrote:
Ok, so for NA observations what is the assumed likelihood function, p(y_i | theta)? Is that the same as for the linear predictor p(eta_i | theta)?

There are no likelihood models at all associated with NA "observations".  They are only used to indicate that there is a linear predictor eta_i that
_would_have_ been associated with an observation if it hadn't been NA.

So for estimation purposes we would have something like this:

p(y | theta) = p(y_1 | theta) x ... x p(y_i | theta) x p(y_i+1 | theta) x ... x p(y_n | theta)

p(y | theta) = Bin(g(eta_1) | theta) x ... x Bin(g(eta_i) | theta) x p(eta_i | theta) x ... x p(eta_n | theta)

Rather, for each "i" for which y_i is not NA,
  p(y_i | eta_i, theta) ~ Bin(Ntrials_i, g^{-1}(eta_i)), conditionally independent across all "i", given eta and theta.

For y_i that is NA  there is no likelihood, and hence no link function, unless the user says that these missing values
_are_ indeed associated with something for which applying the same link function as for the non-NA y_i:s is meaningful.

(At least I think that's the common way of defining the direction of the link function; g(location parameter for y) = linear predictor
It fits the "logit link" language...)

Finn
